title: 2017 AMC 12B Problem 7
statement: The functions \(\sin(x)\) and \(\cos(x)\) are periodic with least period \(2\pi.\) What is the least period of the function \(\cos(\sin(x))?\)

solutions.text:
Since \(\cos(\sin(x + \pi))\) \(= \cos(-\sin(x))\) \(= \cos(\sin(x)),\) the function has period \(\pi.\) It cannot be smaller: \(\cos(\sin(x)) = 1\) exactly when \(\sin(x) = 0,\) which happens only at integer multiples of \(\pi,\) so the maxima are spaced \(\pi\) apart. The least period is \(\pi.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: To rule out a smaller period, note \(\cos(\sin(x)) = 1\) only when \(\sin(x) = 0,\) i.e. at multiples of \(\pi\)
